words.sense: extreme greed for wealth and material gain
misconceptions: Wanting ever more wealth is not automatically resentment of another owner.

words.sense: resentful desire for another person’s possessions or advantages
misconceptions: Resenting another person’s advantage need not involve a hunger for riches.

semantic_axes.description: Avarice is an excessive hunger to acquire wealth itself; envy is resentment directed at what someone else has.

edges.boundary_rule: Avarice is an excessive hunger to acquire wealth itself; envy is resentment directed at what someone else has.
clues_b: comparing oneself bitterly with someone else
irrelevant_clues: whether other people notice the reaction

misconceptions.M1: Wanting ever more wealth is not automatically resentment of another owner.
misconceptions.M2: Resenting another person’s advantage need not involve a hunger for riches.
misconceptions.M3: Do not stick with an old answer after decisive evidence changes, or let surface distractions override the boundary.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amara’s attitude?

beats.text: Amara kept adding to her savings, refusing basic repairs despite having enough money for years.
beats.decisive_clue: accumulating money even at the cost of needs
beats.reason: The desire for more money overrides reasonable needs.

beats.text: She counted the total again after receiving a birthday card.
beats.decisive_clue: accumulating money even at the cost of needs
beats.reason: The card is incidental; the refusal to spend on necessities reveals extreme greed.

chains.feedback_short: Accumulating money even at the cost of needs; the later detail does not change the boundary.
chains.feedback_deep: Avarice concerns extreme greed for wealth and material gain; envy concerns resentful desire for another person’s possessions or advantages. The card is incidental; the refusal to spend on necessities reveals extreme greed.
chains.contrast_rule: Avarice: hoarding wealth without a rival; envy: resenting a friend’s possession.

hints.attention: Consider what she is willing to sacrifice to keep money.
hints.axis: Avarice is an excessive hunger to acquire wealth itself; envy is resentment directed at what someone else has.
hints.contrast: Avarice: hoarding wealth without a rival; envy: resenting a friend’s possession.

beats.text: Rafi frowned when his classmate won the scholarship he had hoped for.
beats.reason: The reaction targets what someone else obtained.

beats.text: He told his sister that seeing the winner celebrate bothered him more than losing the money.
beats.reason: His reaction to the winner, rather than a wish to accumulate cash, fixes the distinction.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Talia’s attitude?

beats.text: Talia bought boxes of collectible coins only to lock them away, saying she could never own enough.
beats.decisive_clue: an insatiable drive to accumulate valuable things
beats.reason: The compulsion concerns acquiring more material value.

beats.text: She photographed each box against a pastel background before locking it away.
beats.decisive_clue: an insatiable drive to accumulate valuable things
beats.reason: The photos do not alter her insatiable drive to acquire and hoard valuables.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Diego’s attitude?

beats.text: Diego saw his neighbour’s beautiful garden and spent days complaining that someone else had a better one.
beats.reason: He is preoccupied with another person having something better.

beats.text: He made those complaints while watering his own healthy plants.
beats.reason: Having his own garden does not erase the resentment toward his neighbour’s.

chains.frame: Which word best describes Nikhil’s attitude?

beats.text: Nikhil canceled promised staff bonuses so he could add the money to his own already enormous earnings.
beats.decisive_clue: taking promised bonuses to increase already enormous personal wealth
beats.reason: His pursuit of additional wealth leads him to take benefits promised to others.

beats.text: He said another million still would not feel like enough.
beats.decisive_clue: taking promised bonuses to increase already enormous personal wealth
beats.reason: His claim that another million would not suffice confirms insatiable greed, not resentment toward another owner.
